VXDNqOJVWH4.text: Fun fact! Revenge bedtime procrastination is the act of staying awake later than you meant to for no valid reason, while at the same time being aware that not going to sleep will negatively affect you in the morning because you know you're going to be tired. The term was first introduced in 2014 by Dutch behavioral scientist Dr. Flor Kroos, who gave it the formal definition of, first, falling asleep is actively delayed, second, there's a lack of a valid reason for staying awake, and third, there's an awareness that not going to sleep will have negative consequences. In a study, 74% of people who were surveyed said they had gone to bed later than they had planned with no valid reason at least once a week. Two explanations are given for why this happens. First, people lack self-control and are addicted to their phones or Netflix and can't make themselves go to sleep. The second explanation is that in our constantly connected busy world, people lack free time for themselves throughout the day, so stealing a few hours of sleep at the end of the day by watching Netflix or scrolling on their phone is what they need to make them feel like they had some me time.

However, I felt really lonely and was doing a horrible job staying connected with friends. I did get much more intentional about calling people and I started responding to texts and batches. Throughout the 30 days, I ended up averaging about 24 minutes of screen time per day, and over two weeks after the challenges ended, I'm now averaging about 45 minutes of screen time, but I feel much more connected with friends. Stop scrolling and engage with the people you care about most.
